# The First Time Founder’s Guide to Employee Background Verification in India


September 18, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[No comments yet](https://salarybox.in/blog/the-first-time-founders-guide-to-employee-background-verification-in-india/#respond)


You have just closed your seed round. Or maybe you are bootstrapping and finally have enough revenue to make your first few hires. Either way, you are about to do something you have probably never done before: build a team from scratch.


There are a hundred things on your plate. Product. Customers. Cash flow. Investor updates. The last thing you want to worry about is whether your new hire’s resume is actually real.


So let me save you some time. This is the no nonsense guide to background verification for first time founders in India. No jargon, no enterprise level complexity, just the practical steps you need to protect your company while moving fast.


#### Why This Matters Even When You Are Small


I know what you are thinking. “We are a five person startup. Background verification is for companies with 500 employees and a compliance department.”


Here is the reality. The cost of a bad hire hits small teams harder than it hits anyone else. When you have five people and one of them turns out to have fabricated their work history, that is 20 percent of your workforce operating under false pretences. The disruption of firing and replacing them burns months of runway, destroys team momentum, and creates a trust deficit that takes time to heal.


Industry data from 2026 puts the average cost of a single bad hire at approximately ₹5 lakhs when you account for lost productivity, rehiring costs, and operational disruption. For a startup burning ₹3 to 5 lakhs a month, that is potentially an entire month of runway gone because of one unverified hire.


The earlier you build verification into your process, the less expensive your mistakes become. And in 2026, the process is simple enough that there is genuinely no reason to skip it.


#### The Only Four Checks You Need to Start


If you have never verified a candidate before, the universe of possible background checks can feel overwhelming. Criminal records, education verification, address checks, social media screening, credit history. Where do you even begin?


Here is the good news. For your first ten to twenty hires, four checks cover the vast majority of hiring risk. Everything else is optional and can be added as your team and your process mature.


**PAN verification** is your identity baseline. The platform checks the candidate’s PAN number against the Income Tax Department database and returns the registered name and date of birth. If those details match what the candidate gave you, you have a foundational identity confirmation from the government itself.


**UAN verification** is your employment history check. The platform accesses EPFO records linked to the candidate’s Universal Account Number and returns actual employer names, PF contribution dates, and amounts. This tells you where the candidate actually worked, when they joined and left, and whether their resume matches government records. For a startup that cannot afford to spend weeks calling previous employers, this single check is worth more than a dozen reference calls.


**Voter ID verification** provides a second independent identity layer. The Election Commission database returns the registered name, date of birth, and address associated with the candidate’s EPIC number. Two government databases confirming the same identity is a much stronger signal than one alone.


**Driving Licence verification** adds a third identity data point and is mandatory for any role involving driving. The VAHAN and SARATHI databases return licence validity, vehicle class authorization, and suspension status.


These four checks, run together, give you a cross referenced identity and employment profile built entirely on government data. It takes minutes and costs a fraction of what you would spend cleaning up after a fraudulent hire.

#### When to Run Checks in Your Hiring Funnel


Timing matters. Run verification too early and you waste money on candidates who will not make it to the offer stage. Run it too late and you create an awkward situation where someone has already accepted your offer before you discover a problem.


The sweet spot for most startups is after the final interview and before extending the offer. At this point, you have already decided this is the person you want. Verification is the last step that confirms your decision is built on solid ground.


For roles where you are choosing between two finalists, run checks on both before making your final call. The verification data might reveal something that tips the decision one way or the other.


Never run verification after onboarding. Discovering a problem after someone has started working, received access to company systems, and begun building relationships with your team is exponentially more expensive and disruptive than catching it during the offer stage.


#### Building the Habit Early


Here is the most important thing I can tell you as a first time founder. The companies that handle background verification well are not the ones with the biggest budgets or the most sophisticated HR departments. They are the ones that made verification a default step from the beginning.


When verification is built into your hiring process from your very first hire, it becomes automatic. Nobody questions it. Nobody skips it. Nobody makes exceptions for candidates who “seem trustworthy.” It is just what your company does.


Compose1 makes this easy because there is nothing to set up, nothing to maintain, and no ongoing commitment. You use it when you need it and it works the same whether you are verifying your third employee or your thirtieth.
